628	`experiments/wildcard/sublinear_correction.py`.
629	
630	In the DCT basis, 99% of delta(n) energy lives in 10.4% of coefficients.
631	**But**: identifying *which* coefficients matter requires having computed
632	delta(n) (mode C), and the dominant indices change with N. Wavelet 99%
633	sparsity scales as N^{0.75} — sublinear, but not polylog.
634	
635	### E6.4 — 90/10 split in sieve update spectrum                      [EVS L]
636	
637	S20; `experiments/wildcard/sieve_function_compression.py`.
638	
639	Sieve update operations have 90% energy in the rank-1 component, while
640	log-Fourier of the sieve function has 90% energy in 10 modes. This is
641	the same smooth-vs-oscillatory split surfacing again — cleanly visible
642	in the **multiplicative-to-additive change of variables** (log-x → mod
643	2*pi/log_x).
644	
645	### E6.5 — Hirsch-Kessler-Mendlovic O~(sqrt(N)) elementary algorithm [EVS M]
646	
647	`literature/state_of_art_2026.md` §1.2; arXiv:2212.09857.
648	
649	First elementary (non-analytic) algorithm matching analytic
650	O(x^{1/2+eps}) — uses Dirichlet convolutions via NTT to speed up the
651	combinatorial side. ~400x slower than primecount in practice but **matches
652	analytic-side asymptotics with no zeta zeros**. A chain that combines
653	HKM with E5.1 (BPSW-TC^0) and E1.3 (carry-boundary) is the closest the
654	project gets to a believable polylog architecture.
655	
656	### E6.6 — Aggarwal 2025 binary search optimality                     [EVS H]
657	
658	`literature/state_of_art_2026.md` §1.4; arXiv:2510.16285.
659	
660	p(n) computable in O(sqrt(n) (log n)^4) unconditionally via binary search
661	on pi(x). **Proves sieve methods CANNOT asymptotically beat
662	binary-search-on-pi(x).** This is *not* polylog, but it is the tightest
663	known upper bound and **explicitly identifies pi(x) as the bottleneck**.
664	
665	> Edge value: **frames the entire research target.** Any polylog p(n)
666	> algorithm reduces (via Aggarwal) to a polylog pi(x) algorithm.
667	
668	---
669	
670	## 7. Negative-but-shape-revealing edges
671	
672	These are not "edges" in the affirmative sense, but they constrain the chain.
673	
674	### E7.1 — Each zeta zero contributes "independent" information     [EVS shape]
675	
676	S25, S45, S20; `experiments/wildcard/zero_sum_acceleration.py`.
677	
678	PSLQ on first 1000-2000 zeros: **0/1225 pairs, 0/4060 triples, 0/400
679	cross-block** integer relations at 30-60 digit precision. Pair-correlation
680	matches GUE to RMS deviation 0.0864. **Zeros are linearly independent
681	over Q in every measurable sense.**
682	
683	### E7.2 — Floor-division is not a ring homomorphism                [EVS shape]
684	
685	S20, S35;
686	`experiments/wildcard/adelic_prime_count_results.md`,
687	`experiments/proposals/proposal17_padic_lifting_results.md`.
688	
689	`floor(x/d) mod q != floor((x mod q)/(d mod q))` — kills ALL purely
690	modular decompositions of pi(x). Every CRT-based attack ultimately
691	trips on this.
692	
693	### E7.3 — Holographic projection: bits are entangled                [EVS shape]
694	
695	S20, S38; `archive/ephemeral/wildcard_findings.md`.
696	
697	For x = 10^{100}, the ~173 "hard" bits of pi(x) are a holographic
698	projection of ~10^{50} zeta-zero contributions. **No single hard bit is
699	independently computable** — every bit needs O(sqrt x) zeros. So per-bit
700	attacks (E1.3 sigmoid) cannot reduce to "compute one bit each, get O(1)
701	per bit."
702	
703	### E7.4 — Inversion iteration is non-contracting                    [EVS shape]
704	
705	S44; `experiments/sieve/inversion_search_results.md`.
706	
707	Fixed-point iteration `p_{k+1} = R^{-1}(n + sum_rho R(p_k^rho))` has
708	|f'| oscillating ~ |sum_rho R'(p^rho)|, which has GUE-random phases,
709	so |f'| is not bounded < 1. Iterating does NOT converge geometrically.
710	**This rules out *any* attempt to "self-correct" R^{-1}(n) using its
711	own truncated zero sum.**
712	
713	### E7.5 — Communication rank caps lower bounds at log^2 x          [EVS shape]
714	
715	S20, S23; `experiments/circuit_complexity/space_time_tradeoff_results.md`.
716	
717	D(pi) ≤ N = log x, so all communication-complexity-based time-space
718	tradeoffs give T*S ≥ Omega(log^2 x), polylog. **The communication route
719	to proving polylog impossible is closed.** Only circuit lower bounds
720	could prove it, and those face Natural Proofs (T4).
721	
722	---
723	
724	## 8. Putative chain templates
725	
726	A chain is a sequence of edges that together produce a polylog
727	architecture for p(n). All chains below have at least one **missing
728	primitive** (clearly labelled), without which they would close. The
729	purpose of catalogueing them is to direct future work at the missing
730	primitives, not to claim a result.
731	
732	### Chain A — Connes operator + R^{-1} + BPSW window         [CLOSED S53; was EVS H]
733	
734	**Status: CLOSED S53 via FOCUS-1 (`experiments/analytic/connes_operator/`).**
735	Step 4 (extending E3.1 to polylog primes) is now provably infeasible by
736	three independent arguments — rank-one parameter count, O(K^3)
737	diagonalization cost, geometric per-zero error growth. The chain
738	described below is preserved for historical reference only.
739	
740	Primitives (historical):
741	1. E6.1: R^{-1}(n) gives top ~60% bits in polylog.
742	2. E1.3: bits beyond R^{-1}(n) need only 4-bit-wide hard zone resolved.
743	3. E3.1: spectral-triple operator built from primes ≤ 13 produces first
744	   50 zeros to 10^{-3} accuracy. **Now downgraded to EVS L.**
745	4. **CLOSED (was MISSING)**: S53 measured K_accurate(B) flat across
746	   B = 1..9 in numerical proxy; analytic arguments close the polylog
747	   regime kernel-independently. CCM's construction is a *one-shot fit*,
748	   not an algorithm.
749	5. E5.1: BPSW gives polylog primality test in the resulting interval.
750	6. E1.2: lag-1 autocorrelation 0.996 means consecutive p(n) values
751	   share most bits — once one anchor is computed, neighbours are cheap.
752	
753	After S53, primitives 1, 2, 5, 6 still hold individually but the chain
754	no longer composes into a polylog architecture.
755	
756	### Chain B — pi(x) mod q polylog → CRT recovery                      [EVS H (no remaining attack surface)]
757	
758	Primitives:
759	1. E3.4: ≤ 6 small moduli {2,3,5,7,11,13} give M = 30030, and the
760	   spectral-truncation interval becomes a *unique* prime under CRT.
761	2. **MISSING**: pi(x) mod q in polylog for q ≤ 13.
762	3. R^{-1}(n) anchor + interval sieve via E5.1 (BPSW polylog).
763	
764	If step 2 existed, the entire problem is solved. Currently pi(x) mod q
765	costs O(x^{1/2+eps}) via L-functions (S21, S22). **The missing
766	primitive is a polylog algorithm for prime-counting in arithmetic
767	progressions for a *constant* small modulus.** This is the cleanest
768	single-target objective the project has produced.
769	
770	**Sub-route closures so far** (do NOT confuse with Chain B itself,
771	which remains compositionally valid; these closures eliminate
772	*specific attempted attacks* on step 2):
773	* Direct L-function: O(x^{1/2+eps}) (S20 line 536, S22 line 568).
774	* Liouville parity (q = 2): closed S46 (identity bottleneck) + S55
775	  (component pseudorandomness under 26-measure battery).
776	* Character-twisted Liouville (q ∈ {3, 5, 7, 11, 13}): closed S56 by
777	  the same dual mechanism — generalised free identity in Z[zeta_d]/2
778	  + pseudorandomness of the next bit (LFSR/N = 0.5000±0.0003 for all
779	  34 chars, max MI < 10⁻⁵ bits with pi(x;q,a) mod 2 for any a). See
780	  `experiments/sieve/pi_mod_q_fixed/character_twisted_liouville.py`,
781	  CLOSED_PATHS line 704, and pseudorandomness measures #27..#31.
782	
783	### Chain C — Liouville parity polylog                               [EVS L (was M, downgraded S55)]
784	
785	Primitives:
786	1. E2.2: identity `pi(x) = (x - L(x))/2 - C_3(x)` is exact.
787	2. **CORRECTED (S55)**: the relevant missing primitive is NOT
788	   `L(x) mod 2` (which is trivially `x mod 2`, free identity), but
789	   either `L(x) mod 4` (= `A(x) mod 2`) OR `C_3(x) mod 2`.
790	3. **STRUCTURALLY CLOSED (S55)**: both components are pseudorandom
791	   under the 26-measure battery (block-entropy saturation, full LFSR
792	   length, FFT z < 6, AC = density bias only) and mutually independent
793	   (MI ~ 2e-5 bits).  See `experiments/sieve/pi_mod_q_fixed/`.
794	4. E5.1: turns pi(x) parity bit + R^{-1} approximation into a polylog
795	   1-bit oracle on intervals of width O(log^2 x) — **but step 2's
796	   primitives are now empirically as hard as pi(x) mod 2 itself.**
797	
798	The chain remains compositionally valid (a polylog algorithm for
799	A(x) mod 2 + a polylog algorithm for C_3(x) mod 2 would still yield
800	pi(x) mod 2), but no structural foothold exists for either component.
801	Razborov-Rudich applies: the empirical pseudorandomness cannot be
802	upgraded to a non-existence proof of polylog circuits.
803	
804	> The Liouville function lambda(n) = (-1)^{Omega(n)} is multiplicative
805	> with simple Dirichlet generating series zeta(2s)/zeta(s). Its
806	> summatory L(x) is **bounded by sqrt x under RH** — directly ties this
807	> chain to the explicit formula. So this chain plausibly reduces to
808	> Chain D's missing primitive (zero-sum compression).
809	
810	### Chain D — Zero-sum collapse via algebraic identity              [EVS M]
811	
812	Primitives:
813	1. E1.1: only O(log x) bits of E(x) need to be extracted.
814	2. E2.7: the rank-deficit "+2" contains *all* the prime-specific
815	   information in the communication matrix.
816	3. **MISSING**: an algebraic identity that collapses
817	   `sum_rho R(x^rho)` to a closed form (analogous to how
818	   `sum_k cos(k theta) = sin((N+1/2)theta)/(2 sin(theta/2)) - 1/2`
819	   collapses many oscillating terms into O(1) operations).
820	4. E3.5: Borel-Padé regularisation hints that the sum has *some*
821	   structure beyond random walk, at least at moderate x.
822	
823	The missing identity is structurally analogous to a generating function
824	or telescoping relation. **This is the "geometric series miracle for
825	zeta zeros" hypothesised in `experiments/wildcard/local_global_reconstruction_results.md`.**
826	PSLQ has been exhaustively searched (S25 + S45) and found nothing of
827	the requisite form, so the identity, if it exists, is not a simple
828	linear combination of the obvious bases.
829	
830	### Chain E — TC^0 via growing-dimension MPOW                        [EVS H]
831	
832	Primitives:
833	1. E5.3: PRIMES in TC^0 ↔ growing-dim MPOW in TC^0.
834	2. E5.1 / E5.2: BPSW or QFT in TC^0 *bypasses* the growing-dim issue
835	   for primality, but not for counting.
836	3. **MISSING**: either resolve growing-dim MPOW in TC^0 (positive),
837	   or find an alternative primitive that turns sieve-style counting
838	   into TC^0.
839	
840	If primes are in TC^0, sum_{k <= x} chi_P(k) is an `x`-input MAJORITY-
841	style threshold counting circuit of size poly(x), depth O(1). To
842	reach polylog *time*, we further need #TC^0 ⊆ NC, which is not known
843	either way. **This is the deepest open frontier of the project.**
844	
845	### Chain F — Aggarwal-style binary search amplification             [EVS L]
846	
847	Primitives:
848	1. E6.6: p(n) reduces to O(log p(n)) calls to pi(·).
849	2. E6.5: pi at one point in O~(sqrt x) elementarily (HKM).
850	3. **MISSING**: any one polylog speedup at *any* step of the chain
851	   — none currently known.
852	
853	This is the "shortest path from current state-of-art to polylog," but
854	each step needs an independent breakthrough. Listed for completeness.
855	
856	### Chain G — Per-bit resolution beyond the carry sigmoid           [EVS M]
857	
858	Primitives:
859	1. E1.3: bits 0..0.6 N are easy; the hard zone is exactly 4 bits wide;
860	   bits 0.6 N+4 .. N are coin-flip.
861	2. E1.2: 0.996 lag-1 autocorrelation in E(x) means a *batch* polylog
862	   algorithm can amortise.
863	3. **MISSING**: a primitive for the 4-bit hard zone — anything that
864	   resolves these 4 bits in polylog would knock pi(x) out of the closed
865	   set.
866	
867	The 4-bit hard zone is so narrow that brute-forcing it with 2^4 = 16
868	hypotheses is "free" — the question is whether any non-trivial polylog
869	operation distinguishes the 16 hypotheses. Sieving the 16 candidates
870	locally is O(polylog) per hypothesis (via E5.1), so verification is
871	free; the bottleneck is the *initial* assignment of each hypothesis to
872	a confidence value, which is exactly the explicit-formula sum.
873	
874	> This chain reduces "polylog pi(x)" to "polylog explicit formula
875	> truncated at 4 bits of accuracy" → ties back to Chains A and D.
876	
877	---
878	
879	## 9. Tactical primitives ready for re-use in chains
880	
881	| Primitive | Cost | Source |
882	|-----------|------|--------|
883	| R^{-1}(n) — Newton inversion of R(x), 50% of digits | O(polylog) | E6.1, V10 algorithm |
884	| Lambert-W Pade approximation, single closed form, 0.019% error | O(1) | `algorithms/v1_pade_approximation.py` |
885	| BPSW primality test (verified to 2^64) | O(polylog) | E5.1 |
886	| Strong Lucas (2x2 MPOW), Jacobi (TC^0) | O(polylog) | E5.1 |
887	| Liouville parity identity verified to x = 10^4 | exact | E2.2 |
888	| Connes operator giving 50 zeros from primes ≤ 13 to 10^{-55..-3} (one-shot fit, not algorithm; see S53) | poly(prime budget) | E3.1 |
889	| Borel-Padé regularisation of explicit formula | constant-factor | E3.5 |
890	| Cesaro-Fejer kernel: 67% recovery at K=100 (vs 53% sharp) | constant-factor | E3.7 |
891	| MPS-base-W identity: rank = min(W^j, phi(W) W^{d-j-1} + 1) | exact | E2.1 |
892	| Wheel-30 + prefetch on Lucy DP | 2-35% | E4.5 |
893	| HKM elementary O~(sqrt x) for pi(x) | O(x^{1/2+eps}) | E6.5 |
894	| Aggarwal binary search: p(n) from pi(x) calls | O(log x) calls | E6.6 |
895	| Bug fix: use mpmath.ei(rho * log x), never li(x**rho) | numerical | E3.6 |
896	| pi(x) mod 2 sign predictable by Chebyshev bias 99.5% | O(1) bits | E3.9 |
897	
898	---
899	
900	## 10. Single-target objectives ranked by "if you cracked this, the
901	   rest of the chain is trivial"
902	
903	1. **Polylog pi(x) mod q for fixed small q** (Chain B). — Highest
904	   value. CRT immediately gives p(n).  All known attack sub-routes
905	   are now closed: direct L-function (S20/S22), Liouville parity for
906	   q=2 (S46/S55), character-twisted Liouville for q in {3,5,7,11,13}
907	   (S56).  Chain B itself remains compositionally valid; the missing
908	   primitive (a polylog algorithm for pi(x;q,a)) has no remaining
909	   identified attack surface.
910	2. **Polylog L(x) mod 4 (= A(x) mod 2) AND C_3(x) mod 2** (Chain C). —
911	   Direct identity exists, but **structurally closed S55**: both bits are
912	   empirically pseudorandom under 26 measures and mutually independent
913	   (MI ~ 2e-5 bits). Free identity L(x) mod 2 = x mod 2 carries no info.
914	   Reduced to L value, since both halves now sit in the
915	   `novel/pseudorandomness_of_pi.md` ledger as measures #25 and #26.
916	3. **Algebraic collapse of the explicit-formula zero sum into closed
917	   form** (Chain D). — High value, low feasibility (PSLQ exhausted).
918	4. **Growing-dim MPOW in TC^0** (Chain E). — Pure complexity-theory
919	   open problem. Affects most strongly *future* chains.
920	5. **A non-AKS TC^0 primality test** (status/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md). —
921	   Eliminates the AKS bottleneck of E5.3.
922	6. **A 4th encoding of pi(x)** (S16). — Three known: prime positions,
923	   zeta zeros, floor values. A fourth, info-equivalent encoding could
924	   sit in TC^0.
925	7. **Connes-operator extension to polylog primes** (E3.1 chain A
926	   step 4). — **CLOSED S53.** Three independent arguments (rank-one
927	   parameter count, O(K^3) diagonalization, geometric per-zero error
928	   growth) rule out polylog scaling kernel-independently. The
929	   "primes ≤ 13 give 50 zeros" result is a one-shot fit, not an
930	   algorithm. See `experiments/analytic/connes_operator/`.
931	
932	---
933	
934	## 11. Reading-list of supporting documents
935	
936	- **The big picture:** `novel/info_computation_gap.md`,
937	  `novel/failure_taxonomy.md`, `novel/pseudorandomness_of_pi.md`.

# EDGES.md — Mathematical Cracks in the sqrt(x) Wall

Vulnerability-research-style catalogue of every **real** mathematical edge,
identity, structural deviation, or partial signal that AI agents have
surfaced over 49 sessions / 690+ closed paths. Listed individually with
exact provenance, then chained into hypothetical attack scenarios.

Conventions:
- **Edge** = a verified mathematical fact, identity, or measurable statistical
  deviation from what a "fully random" object would give. Even if it has
  already failed in isolation, it is recorded here because its value in a
  *chain* is what matters.
- **EVS** (Edge-Value Score, qualitative): H = high (could be a primary
  primitive), M = medium (useful in conjunction), L = low (probably noise but
  recorded for completeness).
- Sources cited as `file:line` or `Sxx` for session number; consult
  `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md` for individual closure entries.

---

## 0. The frame the chain has to fit through

Every chain must address all four targets simultaneously, because a chain that
misses any one of them lands in a known closed path:

T1. **Smooth target (~50% of bits):** R^{-1}(n) gives the top ~60% of the
    bit-length of p(n) in O(polylog) (carry-propagation boundary, S40,
    `novel/carry_propagation_boundary.md`). Any chain that only delivers
    these bits is a duplicate of R^{-1}(n).
T2. **Oscillatory bits (~40%):** the remaining bits encode the GUE-random
    contribution of ~x^{1/2} zeta zeros (`novel/info_computation_gap.md`,
    S36 line 212 of CLOSED_PATHS).
T3. **Avoid the three failure modes:**
    C = "needs primes to compute primes",
    E = "reduces to the explicit formula / O(sqrt x) zero sum",
    I = "smooth approximation loses the oscillatory bits"
    (`novel/failure_taxonomy.md`).
T4. **Avoid the Natural Proofs barrier when reasoning about
    impossibility** — every "natural" structural test we tried gives the
    same answer for chi_P and for a uniformly random Boolean function
    (`novel/pseudorandomness_of_pi.md`, 24 measures).

If a chain ends in "and now compute pi(x;q,a) for q < 13" → C-circular.
If a chain ends in "and now sum sqrt(x) zeta zeros" → E-equivalent.
If a chain ends in "round R(x) + smooth correction" → I-info-loss.

---

## 1. Information-content edges  (these are why the problem might still be open)

### E1.1 — E(x) = pi(x) - Li(x) carries only O(log x) bits        [EVS H]

`novel/info_computation_gap.md`; S36;
`experiments/wildcard/local_global_reconstruction_results.md`.

For x = 10^100, |E(x)| ~ 10^48, so E uses ~160 bits — under 0.15% of the
polylog budget (log2 x)^2 ~ 110,000. **There is NO information-theoretic
barrier to polylog.** The barrier is purely computational: extracting
160 bits from a sum of ~10^50 GUE-random terms with massive cancellation.

> Why this is an "edge": the Razborov-Rudich pseudorandomness picture is
> output-side. On the *input* side, the answer is small. This is the
> primary asymmetry we want to exploit.

### E1.2 — Adjacent-x autocorrelation of the error is 0.996      [EVS M]

`experiments/wildcard/local_global_reconstruction_results.md` Exp 3;
S36; `archive/sessions/session36_synthesis` style block.

`Corr(E(x), E(x+1)) = 0.996` and `std(E(x+1)-E(x)) = 0.326`.  Helpless for
*single-point* p(n) computation, but **very useful for batch / sliding /
oracle-amortised algorithms**: a single anchor pi(x_0) plus 0.326-std
local increments determines pi at neighbouring points.

### E1.3 — Per-bit difficulty of p(n) is a sharp 4-bit sigmoid    [EVS H]

`novel/carry_propagation_boundary.md`; S40
`experiments/wildcard/carry_propagation_boundary.py`.

Bit positions 0-7 (MSB) match round(R^{-1}(n)) at ≥95%. Positions 8-9
are 80-90%. From bit 10 onward, agreement is 50% (coin flip). Width of
the "hard zone" is *only ~4 bits* and located at ~60% from MSB. For
N-bit p(n), the hard region is bits 0.6·N .. N (asymptotic).

> Why this is an edge: the hard region has a sharp boundary, not a long
> tail. A method that produces *any* extra bit beyond R^{-1}(n)'s ceiling
> is enough — you don't have to break the whole barrier, only the first
> bit past the cliff.

### E1.4 — N/2 universality                                        [EVS M]

`novel/pseudorandomness_of_pi.md` table; `novel/approx_degree_prime.md`;
S28 synthesis. Five independent measures land on the same threshold:

| Measure                             | Boundary       | Source |
|-------------------------------------|----------------|--------|
| Approximate degree of chi_P at eps=0.49 | ceil(N/2)  | S28 |
| Communication matrix rank           | 2^{N/2-1}+2    | S17 |
| PTF (polynomial-threshold) degree   | N/2 (LP-verified, N=4..12) | S35 |
| LFSR length over GF(p) for delta(n) | N/2            | S24,S26 |
| Per-bit R-correlation crossover     | ~bit N/2       | S28 |
| Real tensor rank of chi_P (3-way)   | ~d^{1.5}=2^{N/2} | S31 |

Empirically: bits 0..N/2 are oscillatory, bits N/2..N are smooth.
**This is not a barrier per se; it's a bisection of the problem into a
solved half (smooth) and an unsolved half (oscillatory).**

---

## 2. Algebraic edges  (small but non-zero structural deviations from random)

### E2.1 — TT (MPS) bond-dim identity at every primorial cut       [EVS H]

`novel/mps_bond_dimension.md`; S41/S42; `experiments/wildcard/mps_bond_dimension*.md`.

For the prime indicator chi_P : [1, W^d] → {0,1} reshaped in base W:

```
   rank M^{(j)} = min( W^j , phi(W) * W^{d-j-1} + 1 )
```

at *every* cut 1 ≤ j < d, *every* primorial W ≥ 2. Empirically saturated to

### E2.2 — Liouville/parity identity                                [EVS M (was H, downgraded S55)]

S46, S55; `experiments/proposals/proposal25_liouville_parity_check.py`
and `experiments/sieve/pi_mod_q_fixed/liouville_modular_structure.py`.

```
   pi(x) = (x - L(x)) / 2 - C_3(x)
```

where `L(x) = sum_{n<=x} (-1)^{Omega(n)}` is the Liouville summatory and
`C_3(x) = #{n <= x : Omega(n) odd, Omega(n) >= 3}`. **Verified exactly for

~3·pi(x) and parity-tests pseudorandom against simple proxies.

(since L is a sum of x terms each in {+1,-1}, parity = count parity).
So L(x) mod 2 carries ZERO non-trivial prime information.  The S46
quote "polylog L(x) mod 2 → polylog pi(x) mod 2" is vacuously satisfied
without yielding a new bit.

The actual missing primitives via E2.2 are:

* `L(x) mod 4` (equivalently `A(x) mod 2 = (x - L(x))/2 mod 2`), AND
* `C_3(x) mod 2`,

with `pi(x) mod 2 = A(x) mod 2 XOR C_3(x) mod 2` (verified bit-exact on
x ∈ [1, 2 000 000]).

S55 measured both components on x up to 2 × 10⁶ and found:

* A(x) mod 2 has block-entropy 7.9999/8 bits, AC-max[1..30] = 0.0010,
  FFT z = 5.5 (no spectral line), GF(2) LFSR length = N/2 — *more*
  pseudorandom than pi(x) mod 2 itself.
* C_3(x) mod 2 has block-entropy 7.88/8, AC = 0.148 (density bias only),
  GF(2) LFSR length = N/2.
* Mutual information I(A mod 2; C_3 mod 2) ≈ 2 × 10⁻⁵ bits — the two
  are statistically independent.
* 11 cheap arithmetic proxies (M(x), Q(x), is_square(x), x mod 4, ...)
  all show |corr| < 0.002 with pi(x) mod 2; best XOR-fusion of any
  4-subset achieves 0.4951 agreement (worse than chance).

> *each* structurally pseudorandom (LFSR, AC, FFT, MI) and *mutually

These are not "edges" in the affirmative sense, but they constrain the chain.

### E7.1 — Each zeta zero contributes "independent" information     [EVS shape]

S25, S45, S20; `experiments/wildcard/zero_sum_acceleration.py`.

PSLQ on first 1000-2000 zeros: **0/1225 pairs, 0/4060 triples, 0/400
cross-block** integer relations at 30-60 digit precision. Pair-correlation
matches GUE to RMS deviation 0.0864. **Zeros are linearly independent
over Q in every measurable sense.**

### E7.2 — Floor-division is not a ring homomorphism                [EVS shape]

S20, S35;
`experiments/wildcard/adelic_prime_count_results.md`,
`experiments/proposals/proposal17_padic_lifting_results.md`.

`floor(x/d) mod q != floor((x mod q)/(d mod q))` — kills ALL purely
modular decompositions of pi(x). Every CRT-based attack ultimately
trips on this.

### E7.3 — Holographic projection: bits are entangled                [EVS shape]

S20, S38; `archive/ephemeral/wildcard_findings.md`.

For x = 10^{100}, the ~173 "hard" bits of pi(x) are a holographic
projection of ~10^{50} zeta-zero contributions. **No single hard bit is
independently computable** — every bit needs O(sqrt x) zeros. So per-bit
attacks (E1.3 sigmoid) cannot reduce to "compute one bit each, get O(1)
per bit."

### E7.4 — Inversion iteration is non-contracting                    [EVS shape]

S44; `experiments/sieve/inversion_search_results.md`.

Fixed-point iteration `p_{k+1} = R^{-1}(n + sum_rho R(p_k^rho))` has
|f'| oscillating ~ |sum_rho R'(p^rho)|, which has GUE-random phases,
so |f'| is not bounded < 1. Iterating does NOT converge geometrically.
**This rules out *any* attempt to "self-correct" R^{-1}(n) using its
own truncated zero sum.**

### E7.5 — Communication rank caps lower bounds at log^2 x          [EVS shape]

S20, S23; `experiments/circuit_complexity/space_time_tradeoff_results.md`.

D(pi) ≤ N = log x, so all communication-complexity-based time-space
tradeoffs give T*S ≥ Omega(log^2 x), polylog. **The communication route
to proving polylog impossible is closed.** Only circuit lower bounds
could prove it, and those face Natural Proofs (T4).

---

## 8. Putative chain templates

A chain is a sequence of edges that together produce a polylog
architecture for p(n). All chains below have at least one **missing
primitive** (clearly labelled), without which they would close. The
purpose of catalogueing them is to direct future work at the missing
primitives, not to claim a result.

### Chain A — Connes operator + R^{-1} + BPSW window         [CLOSED S53; was EVS H]

**Status: CLOSED S53 via FOCUS-1 (`experiments/analytic/connes_operator/`).**
Step 4 (extending E3.1 to polylog primes) is now provably infeasible by
three independent arguments — rank-one parameter count, O(K^3)
diagonalization cost, geometric per-zero error growth. The chain
described below is preserved for historical reference only.

Primitives (historical):
1. E6.1: R^{-1}(n) gives top ~60% bits in polylog.
2. E1.3: bits beyond R^{-1}(n) need only 4-bit-wide hard zone resolved.
3. E3.1: spectral-triple operator built from primes ≤ 13 produces first
   50 zeros to 10^{-3} accuracy. **Now downgraded to EVS L.**
4. **CLOSED (was MISSING)**: S53 measured K_accurate(B) flat across
   B = 1..9 in numerical proxy; analytic arguments close the polylog
   regime kernel-independently. CCM's construction is a *one-shot fit*,
   not an algorithm.
5. E5.1: BPSW gives polylog primality test in the resulting interval.
6. E1.2: lag-1 autocorrelation 0.996 means consecutive p(n) values
   share most bits — once one anchor is computed, neighbours are cheap.

After S53, primitives 1, 2, 5, 6 still hold individually but the chain
no longer composes into a polylog architecture.

### Chain B — pi(x) mod q polylog → CRT recovery                      [EVS H (no remaining attack surface)]

Primitives:
1. E3.4: ≤ 6 small moduli {2,3,5,7,11,13} give M = 30030, and the
   spectral-truncation interval becomes a *unique* prime under CRT.
2. **MISSING**: pi(x) mod q in polylog for q ≤ 13.
3. R^{-1}(n) anchor + interval sieve via E5.1 (BPSW polylog).

If step 2 existed, the entire problem is solved. Currently pi(x) mod q
costs O(x^{1/2+eps}) via L-functions (S21, S22). **The missing
primitive is a polylog algorithm for prime-counting in arithmetic
progressions for a *constant* small modulus.** This is the cleanest
single-target objective the project has produced.

**Sub-route closures so far** (do NOT confuse with Chain B itself,
which remains compositionally valid; these closures eliminate
*specific attempted attacks* on step 2):
* Direct L-function: O(x^{1/2+eps}) (S20 line 536, S22 line 568).
* Liouville parity (q = 2): closed S46 (identity bottleneck) + S55
  (component pseudorandomness under 26-measure battery).
* Character-twisted Liouville (q ∈ {3, 5, 7, 11, 13}): closed S56 by
  the same dual mechanism — generalised free identity in Z[zeta_d]/2
  + pseudorandomness of the next bit (LFSR/N = 0.5000±0.0003 for all
  34 chars, max MI < 10⁻⁵ bits with pi(x;q,a) mod 2 for any a). See
  `experiments/sieve/pi_mod_q_fixed/character_twisted_liouville.py`,
  CLOSED_PATHS line 704, and pseudorandomness measures #27..#31.

### Chain C — Liouville parity polylog                               [EVS L (was M, downgraded S55)]

Primitives:
1. E2.2: identity `pi(x) = (x - L(x))/2 - C_3(x)` is exact.
2. **CORRECTED (S55)**: the relevant missing primitive is NOT
   `L(x) mod 2` (which is trivially `x mod 2`, free identity), but
   either `L(x) mod 4` (= `A(x) mod 2`) OR `C_3(x) mod 2`.
3. **STRUCTURALLY CLOSED (S55)**: both components are pseudorandom
   under the 26-measure battery (block-entropy saturation, full LFSR
   length, FFT z < 6, AC = density bias only) and mutually independent
   (MI ~ 2e-5 bits).  See `experiments/sieve/pi_mod_q_fixed/`.
4. E5.1: turns pi(x) parity bit + R^{-1} approximation into a polylog
   1-bit oracle on intervals of width O(log^2 x) — **but step 2's
   primitives are now empirically as hard as pi(x) mod 2 itself.**

The chain remains compositionally valid (a polylog algorithm for
A(x) mod 2 + a polylog algorithm for C_3(x) mod 2 would still yield
pi(x) mod 2), but no structural foothold exists for either component.
Razborov-Rudich applies: the empirical pseudorandomness cannot be
upgraded to a non-existence proof of polylog circuits.

> The Liouville function lambda(n) = (-1)^{Omega(n)} is multiplicative
> with simple Dirichlet generating series zeta(2s)/zeta(s). Its
> summatory L(x) is **bounded by sqrt x under RH** — directly ties this
> chain to the explicit formula. So this chain plausibly reduces to
> Chain D's missing primitive (zero-sum compression).

### Chain D — Zero-sum collapse via algebraic identity              [EVS M]

Primitives:
1. E1.1: only O(log x) bits of E(x) need to be extracted.
2. E2.7: the rank-deficit "+2" contains *all* the prime-specific
   information in the communication matrix.
3. **MISSING**: an algebraic identity that collapses
   `sum_rho R(x^rho)` to a closed form (analogous to how
   `sum_k cos(k theta) = sin((N+1/2)theta)/(2 sin(theta/2)) - 1/2`
   collapses many oscillating terms into O(1) operations).
4. E3.5: Borel-Padé regularisation hints that the sum has *some*
   structure beyond random walk, at least at moderate x.

The missing identity is structurally analogous to a generating function
or telescoping relation. **This is the "geometric series miracle for
zeta zeros" hypothesised in `experiments/wildcard/local_global_reconstruction_results.md`.**
PSLQ has been exhaustively searched (S25 + S45) and found nothing of
the requisite form, so the identity, if it exists, is not a simple
linear combination of the obvious bases.

### Chain E — TC^0 via growing-dimension MPOW                        [EVS H]

Primitives:
1. E5.3: PRIMES in TC^0 ↔ growing-dim MPOW in TC^0.
2. E5.1 / E5.2: BPSW or QFT in TC^0 *bypasses* the growing-dim issue
   for primality, but not for counting.
3. **MISSING**: either resolve growing-dim MPOW in TC^0 (positive),
   or find an alternative primitive that turns sieve-style counting
   into TC^0.

If primes are in TC^0, sum_{k <= x} chi_P(k) is an `x`-input MAJORITY-
style threshold counting circuit of size poly(x), depth O(1). To
reach polylog *time*, we further need #TC^0 ⊆ NC, which is not known
either way. **This is the deepest open frontier of the project.**

### Chain F — Aggarwal-style binary search amplification             [EVS L]

Primitives:
1. E6.6: p(n) reduces to O(log p(n)) calls to pi(·).
2. E6.5: pi at one point in O~(sqrt x) elementarily (HKM).
3. **MISSING**: any one polylog speedup at *any* step of the chain
   — none currently known.

This is the "shortest path from current state-of-art to polylog," but
each step needs an independent breakthrough. Listed for completeness.

### Chain G — Per-bit resolution beyond the carry sigmoid           [EVS M]

Primitives:
1. E1.3: bits 0..0.6 N are easy; the hard zone is exactly 4 bits wide;
   bits 0.6 N+4 .. N are coin-flip.
2. E1.2: 0.996 lag-1 autocorrelation in E(x) means a *batch* polylog
   algorithm can amortise.
3. **MISSING**: a primitive for the 4-bit hard zone — anything that
   resolves these 4 bits in polylog would knock pi(x) out of the closed
   set.

The 4-bit hard zone is so narrow that brute-forcing it with 2^4 = 16
hypotheses is "free" — the question is whether any non-trivial polylog
operation distinguishes the 16 hypotheses. Sieving the 16 candidates
locally is O(polylog) per hypothesis (via E5.1), so verification is
free; the bottleneck is the *initial* assignment of each hypothesis to
a confidence value, which is exactly the explicit-formula sum.

> This chain reduces "polylog pi(x)" to "polylog explicit formula
> truncated at 4 bits of accuracy" → ties back to Chains A and D.

---

## 9. Tactical primitives ready for re-use in chains

| Primitive | Cost | Source |
|-----------|------|--------|
| R^{-1}(n) — Newton inversion of R(x), 50% of digits | O(polylog) | E6.1, V10 algorithm |
| Lambert-W Pade approximation, single closed form, 0.019% error | O(1) | `algorithms/v1_pade_approximation.py` |
| BPSW primality test (verified to 2^64) | O(polylog) | E5.1 |
| Strong Lucas (2x2 MPOW), Jacobi (TC^0) | O(polylog) | E5.1 |
| Liouville parity identity verified to x = 10^4 | exact | E2.2 |
| Connes operator giving 50 zeros from primes ≤ 13 to 10^{-55..-3} (one-shot fit, not algorithm; see S53) | poly(prime budget) | E3.1 |
| Borel-Padé regularisation of explicit formula | constant-factor | E3.5 |
| Cesaro-Fejer kernel: 67% recovery at K=100 (vs 53% sharp) | constant-factor | E3.7 |
| MPS-base-W identity: rank = min(W^j, phi(W) W^{d-j-1} + 1) | exact | E2.1 |
| Wheel-30 + prefetch on Lucy DP | 2-35% | E4.5 |
| HKM elementary O~(sqrt x) for pi(x) | O(x^{1/2+eps}) | E6.5 |
| Aggarwal binary search: p(n) from pi(x) calls | O(log x) calls | E6.6 |
| Bug fix: use mpmath.ei(rho * log x), never li(x**rho) | numerical | E3.6 |
| pi(x) mod 2 sign predictable by Chebyshev bias 99.5% | O(1) bits | E3.9 |

---

## 10. Single-target objectives ranked by "if you cracked this, the
   rest of the chain is trivial"

1. **Polylog pi(x) mod q for fixed small q** (Chain B). — Highest
   value. CRT immediately gives p(n).  All known attack sub-routes
   are now closed: direct L-function (S20/S22), Liouville parity for
   q=2 (S46/S55), character-twisted Liouville for q in {3,5,7,11,13}
   (S56).  Chain B itself remains compositionally valid; the missing
   primitive (a polylog algorithm for pi(x;q,a)) has no remaining
   identified attack surface.
2. **Polylog L(x) mod 4 (= A(x) mod 2) AND C_3(x) mod 2** (Chain C). —
   Direct identity exists, but **structurally closed S55**: both bits are
   empirically pseudorandom under 26 measures and mutually independent
   (MI ~ 2e-5 bits). Free identity L(x) mod 2 = x mod 2 carries no info.
   Reduced to L value, since both halves now sit in the
   `novel/pseudorandomness_of_pi.md` ledger as measures #25 and #26.
3. **Algebraic collapse of the explicit-formula zero sum into closed
   form** (Chain D). — High value, low feasibility (PSLQ exhausted).
4. **Growing-dim MPOW in TC^0** (Chain E). — Pure complexity-theory
   open problem. Affects most strongly *future* chains.
5. **A non-AKS TC^0 primality test** (status/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md). —
   Eliminates the AKS bottleneck of E5.3.
6. **A 4th encoding of pi(x)** (S16). — Three known: prime positions,
   zeta zeros, floor values. A fourth, info-equivalent encoding could
   sit in TC^0.
7. **Connes-operator extension to polylog primes** (E3.1 chain A
   step 4). — **CLOSED S53.** Three independent arguments (rank-one
   parameter count, O(K^3) diagonalization, geometric per-zero error
   growth) rule out polylog scaling kernel-independently. The
   "primes ≤ 13 give 50 zeros" result is a one-shot fit, not an
   algorithm. See `experiments/analytic/connes_operator/`.

---

## 11. Reading-list of supporting documents

- **The big picture:** `novel/info_computation_gap.md`,
  `novel/failure_taxonomy.md`, `novel/pseudorandomness_of_pi.md`.
- **What's proven hard:** `proven/circuit_size_barrier.md`,
  `proven/uniformity_barrier.md`,
  `proven/convergence_acceleration_barrier.md`,
  `proven/workspace_mismatch_barrier.md`.
- **The only open frontier:** `status/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md`,
  `novel/tc0_matrix_powering_reduction.md`,
  `novel/bpsw_tc0_reduction.md`,
  `literature/matrix_powering_tc0.md`.
- **The bisection at N/2:** `novel/approx_degree_prime.md`,
  `novel/carry_propagation_boundary.md`, `novel/delta_spectrum.md`.
- **The MPS theorem:** `novel/mps_bond_dimension.md`.
- **The Liouville identity:** `experiments/proposals/proposal25_liouville_parity_check.py` and `_results.md`.
- **The Connes spectral triple:** `literature/state_of_art_2026.md` §2.5b.
- **Bug to avoid:** `experiments/proposals/proposal26_fejer_damped_explicit.py` (mpmath.ei vs li branch cut).

---

4	- **A** — Reordered tensor-train compression of `delta(n)` across 7 orderings;
5	- **B** — LASSO compressed-sensing of `delta(n)` in the zero-mode basis;
6	- **C** — Learned (ridge) residues at fixed zeta zeros.

9	critique:
10	
11	1. cross-checks each against `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md` (705 lines / 533+ entries),
12	   citing the exact prior closures (most are pre-Session-49);
13	2. flags **Proposal C's basis misspecification** (cos(γ log n)/√n uses prime
14	   *index* n, but the explicit-formula basis is in prime *value* p(n));
15	3. runs the corrected basis and confirms the negative verdict survives;

22	## A — Reordered TT compression of delta(n)
23	
24	**Verdict: DUPLICATE — the multi-ordering test is a refinement, not a new
25	mechanism. All seven orderings produce identical volume-law saturation,
26	confirming line 171's S10 closure is ordering-independent.**
27	
28	**CLOSED_PATHS adjacency:**
29	
30	| Line | Entry | Match |
31	|------|-------|-------|
32	| 171  | MPS / tensor network — FAIL/I; bond dim ~ N^{0.49}, volume-law (S10) | EXACT mechanism (natural ordering only) |
33	| 185  | Tensor sieve (MPS of divisibility DFAs) — FAIL/I (S20) | Adjacent: DFA-product variant |
34	| 516  | Tensor network / MPS sieve — FAIL/I; bond = primorial (S20) | Adjacent: sieve-not-delta variant |
35	| 517  | MPS bond dim of chi_P at base-W half cut — FAIL/E; theorem gives rank = min(W^j, φ(W)·W^{d-j-1}+1) (S41) | Theorem-level closure for any base |
36	| 599  | Tensor network MPS Legendre sieve contraction — FAIL/I; bond ~ 2^{0.33-0.43·a} (S26) | Adjacent: sieve-state target |
37	
38	**The new measurement.** At N=2^13=8192, eps_rel=1e-3 SVD truncation, **all
39	seven orderings** (identity, bit-reversal, Gray, Morton, 2-adic, sort_by_R^{-1},
40	random) plus Gaussian noise produce **identical** bond profiles
41	`[2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2]`. The smooth-cosine positive
42	control achieves bond-dim 2 throughout, confirming the SVD pipeline is
43	sensitive to structure when present.
44	
45	**Why the new test does not break the closure.** The bond profile
46	`[2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 64, 32, …, 2]` is the *mathematical maximum* at each
47	cut for a binary L=13 TT (cut k bonded by min(2^k, 2^{L-k})). Saturating
48	this at threshold 1e-3 is necessary but not sufficient for volume-law; the
49	gaussian-noise baseline saturates the same ceiling, indicating delta is
50	indistinguishable from GUE noise at this resolution. Tighter thresholds
51	(1e-6, 1e-9) would still fail to expose structure: line 24 (S25) shows
52	DFT spectral flatness 0.93–0.999 on zeros, so any reorthogonalization of
53	delta inherits a flat singular-value spectrum.
54	
55	**Independent re-derivation.** Theorem in line 517 establishes the chi_P
56	bond-dim at every cut for any base-W half-cut; the new test is the same
57	formula instantiated for W=2 with index permutations, all of which give
58	the W=2 ceiling 2^min(j, L-j). Bit-reversal/Gray/Morton are 2-adic
59	isomorphisms of the binary cube and cannot change the half-cut min;
60	sort_by_R^{-1} reorders R^{-1}(n) into a near-monotone curve but the
61	*residual* delta = p(n) - R^{-1}(n) is GUE-random regardless of how the
62	indices are sorted. The 7-ordering test cannot succeed because the
63	residual after smooth subtraction is invariant under any
64	order-preserving sort applied to the sum, and bit-permutation orderings
65	permute *labels* without changing the SVD spectrum of the multilinear
66	contraction.
67	
68	**Useful refinement to keep.** The seven-ordering identical-saturation
69	result is the most explicit statement of "volume-law is ordering-independent
70	under binary TT" the project has on record. **Bond profile
71	`[2,4,8,16,32,64,64,32,16,8,4,2]` is the binary-TT volume-law fingerprint**
72	across N=8192 and all seven tested orderings.
73	
74	**Failure mode:** I (information-theoretic).
75	
76	**Action:** add CLOSED_PATHS entry sharpening line 171 with the seven-ordering
77	identical-saturation result.

81	## B — LASSO compressed-sensing on zero-mode basis
82	
83	**Verdict: DUPLICATE — direct hit on TWO existing CLOSED_PATHS entries.**
84	
85	**CLOSED_PATHS adjacency (in age order):**
86	
87	| Line | Entry | Match |
88	|------|-------|-------|
89	| 350  | Compressed sensing on K zeros — PARTIAL/I; "lucky cancellations small x, doesn't scale" (S7) | EXACT mechanism, original closure |
90	| **699** | **Compressed-sensing recovery of psi(x) via random K-subset of zeta zeros** — FAIL/E; first-K is near-optimal among K-subsets, signal DENSE in zero basis with smoothly-decaying amplitudes (S54) | **EXACT mechanism, last-session closure** |
91	| 623  | Compressed sensing on prime indicator — FAIL/C; "99% energy in 1.25% Fourier components but those ARE zeta zero frequencies. Circular." (S29) | Adjacent: prime-indicator target |
92	| 472  | Goldreich-Levin / list decoding for pi(x) — FAIL/I; commrank 2^{N/2} blocks any sparse Fourier recovery (S18) | Structural: blocks any sparse-basis route |
93	| 240  | Wavelet/Fourier compression of correction C(x) — FAIL/I; 99.9% energy needs N^{0.75} coefs (S40) | Adjacent: same target signal |
94	| 653  | Contour integral evaluation of zero sum — FAIL/E; "99% energy needs 133/500 components. No sparse representation in any basis." (S32) | Adjacent: same basis, different fitness |
95	
96	**The new measurement.** At N=4096, K_max=1024, alpha sweep
97	{1e-6, …, 1e-1}, the LASSO best-test-RMSE solution at every K and every
98	alpha is **nnz=0** (predict delta=0). OLS overfits catastrophically at
99	K≥256 (test RMSE blows up to 1e10). The naive `round(R^{-1})` baseline
100	matches the all-zero LASSO at 1.1% prime recovery.
101	
102	**Independent verification of the proposer's negative.**
103	Line 699 last session ran a closely-related test: random K=50 subsets of
104	2000 zeros for psi(x) recovery, finding random-subsets STRICTLY WORSE than
105	first-K (rms 404 vs 97, 4× worse). Conclusion: signal is dense in zero
106	basis with 1/|rho_k|-decaying amplitudes, **not K-sparse**. LASSO on the
107	same basis with no amplitude prior simply discovers the same fact in a
108	weaker form: every coefficient must scale ~1/|rho_k| to match the
109	analytic explicit formula, so L1-promoting sparsity is unable to prefer
110	any small subset.
111	
112	The sklearn LASSO at alpha=1e-1 is sufficiently aggressive to zero
113	everything. At alpha=1e-6, the model approaches OLS and overfits as soon
114	as K > N_train/2 = 1024. There is no mid-alpha sweet spot because there
115	is no actual sparsity to discover.

117	**Failure mode:** I (information-theoretic) reinforced by E (signal has no
118	sparse basis representation by line 699 evidence).

120	**Action:** add CLOSED_PATHS entry refining line 350 with the LASSO
121	all-zero outcome and line 699 cross-reference.

125	## C — Learned (ridge) residues at fixed zeta zeros
126	
127	**Verdict: DUPLICATE + FLAWED BASIS — the proposer's basis
128	`cos(γ log n)/√n` uses the prime *index* n, but the explicit-formula's
129	natural variable is the prime *value* p(n). The qualitative conclusion
130	survives the correction (verified empirically below), but the experiment
131	as written does not test what it claims.**
132	
133	### The basis-misspecification flaw
134	
135	The explicit formula gives
136	`f(x) = π(x) − R(x) ≈ −2√x/log x · Σ_k cos(γ_k log x − φ_k)/|ρ_k|`.
137	
138	Inverting around the prime sequence: for `δ(n) = p(n) − R^{-1}(n)`,
139	linearizing R^{-1} at n gives
140	`δ(n) ≈ f(p_n) · log(p_n) ≈ −2√p_n · Σ_k cos(γ_k log p_n − φ_k)/|ρ_k|`.
141	
142	The natural ridge basis is therefore **`{√p_n · cos(γ_k log p_n),
143	√p_n · sin(γ_k log p_n)}`** — uses prime *value* p_n (not index n) and
144	amplitude `√p_n` (not `1/√n`). The proposer used `cos(γ log n)/√n`, which
145	is the *wrong* basis: amplitude scales like `1/√n` ≈ `1/√(N/log N)`
146	instead of the correct `√p_n` ≈ `√(N log N)` (a factor of N off).
147	
148	### Critic experiment with corrected basis
149	
150	`experiments/proposals/critique49_basis_misspec.py` runs ridge regression
151	under both bases at K ∈ {32, 128, 512, 2000} on the same train/test split.
152	
153	| K | orig acc | correct acc | orig test RMSE | correct test RMSE |
154	|---|---|---|---|---|
155	| 32 | 0.015 | 0.014 | 37.40 | **25.32** |
156	| 128 | 0.011 | 0.017 | 37.39 | **23.66** |
157	| 512 | 0.012 | 0.000 | 38.12 | 1670.74 |
158	| 2000 | 0.011 | 0.000 | 38.27 | 795.42 |
159	
160	Naive baseline: 0.011.
161	
162	**Findings:**
163	- Correct basis gives strictly lower test RMSE at K=32, 128 (25.3 vs 37.4;
164	  23.7 vs 37.4) — the correct basis IS more informative.
165	- Correct basis catastrophically overfits at K ≥ 512 — same overfitting
166	  pattern as OLS, regularization cannot save it.
167	- **Even the most-informative correct basis at K=128 gives 1.7% recovery,
168	  ≈naive 1.1%** — RMSE 23.7 means predictions are off by ±24 on average,
169	  far above the 0.5 rounding threshold.
170	
171	**The basis misspecification did NOT hide a positive result.** Proposal C
172	closes under both the original and the corrected basis.
173	
174	### CLOSED_PATHS adjacency for the underlying mechanism
175	
176	| Line | Entry | Match |
177	|------|-------|-------|
178	| 145  | Deep ML (ridge/AR) — FAIL/I; 5.4% test exact (S8) | Direct mechanism: ML on delta |
179	| 561  | ML (Ridge/kNN) prediction of delta(n) — FAIL/I; 0% exact on 1000 test cases (S21) | EXACT: ridge on delta |
180	| 622  | Polynomial empirical correction to R(x) — FAIL/I; "Polynomial in 1/log(x) reduces error 60-80% but cross-validation confirms overfitting" (S29) | Adjacent: learned coefficients on a fixed basis |
181	| 664  | Spectral truncation / adaptive zero selection — FAIL/E; "1000 zeros insufficient for n≥500" (S33) | Adjacent: same basis, no learned coefs |
182	| **691** | **Extended PSLQ basis for f(x) — 10 zeta-zero modes** — FAIL/I; cross-check residuals 4e2-6e3 (S48) | EXACT basis structure |
183	| **692** | **Hermite/Gaussian/Riesz mollification of explicit formula** — FAIL/E; mollification at most 1.21x better (S48) | Direct: re-weighted-coefficient variant |
184	| **702** | **PSLQ + structured zeta-zero/log basis on delta(n) (8th PSLQ-on-delta)** — FAIL/I+E (S49 round 1) | Direct: PSLQ-coefficient variant of same atoms |
185	
186	**Why no learned-coefficient choice can break the bound (re-derivation).**
187	The truncation tail beyond K zeros has L^2 norm
188	`≥ Σ_{k>K} 1/(γ_k^2) ~ 1/(K log K)`. Multiplying by the `√p_n` amplitude
189	gives an irreducible test-RMSE floor of `Ω(√(p_n)/(√K · √log K))`. At
190	N=4096, p_N≈40000, K=2000, this floor is `~ √40000/√(2000·7.6) ~ 1.6`, so
191	ridge plateaus near naïve no matter what coefficients are learned within
192	the kept-K subspace.
193	
194	The "learned coefficients can absorb tail energy" hypothesis is
195	**provably false in L^2**: the tail energy is orthogonal to the kept-K
196	subspace, so the L^2-optimal kept-K coefficients are exactly the analytic
197	1/ρ residues, and any data-fit deviates further from the truth on the
198	test window. This is why the proposer found **at most 0.4pp** gap
199	between analytic and ridge: that gap is finite-sample noise.
200	
201	**Failure mode:** I (information-theoretic) — same as line 691, 692.
202	
203	**Action:** add CLOSED_PATHS entry refining lines 691 and 692 with the
204	ridge-vs-analytic null gap and the basis-misspecification correction.
205

208	## Summary
209	
210	| Proposal | Verdict   | Failure Mode | Strict prior closure | New CLOSED_PATHS entry? |
211	|----------|-----------|--------------|----------------------|--------------------------|
212	| **A — Reordered TT** | DUPLICATE | I | line 171 (S10) | YES (refines: 7 orderings identically saturate volume-law ceiling at N=8192) |
213	| **B — LASSO on zero modes** | DUPLICATE | I | lines 350 (S7), **699 (S54)** | YES (refines: LASSO best-test-RMSE = nnz=0 at every K, alpha) |
214	| **C — Learned residues** | DUPLICATE + FLAWED BASIS | I | lines 561 (S21), 691/692 (S48), 702 (S49 R1) | YES (refines: corrected `√p_n · cos(γ log p_n)` basis still plateaus at naïve) |
215	
216	**No proposal survived critique with a polylog or sub-√x route to π(x).**
217	All three close to entries that pre-date this session — Proposal B's mechanism
218	was last closed *last session* (line 699, S54), suggesting the proposer-mode
219	prompt failed to surface the most recent CLOSED_PATHS entries.
220	
221	**Process note.** Proposal A's seven-ordering test is the strongest empirical
222	"ordering-independent volume-law" demonstration on record — preserve as a
223	refinement. Proposal B's LASSO discovers L1-sparsity is impossible by getting
224	nnz=0 — duplicate of S54 line 699 but worth recording. Proposal C contains
225	a basis-misspecification flaw (uses prime index n instead of prime value
226	p_n); critic re-ran the corrected basis and confirms the closure stands.
227	
228	**Open status unchanged.** The only genuinely open avenue per
229	`status/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md` is **circuit complexity of π(x)** (Berry–Keating /
230	TC^0 lower-bound monitoring). All three proposals attack the analytic /
231	information-loss side; none addresses circuit complexity.
232	
233	**Process recommendation.** The proposer wrote `cos(γ log n)/√n` from
234	memory, not from the explicit-formula derivation. A pre-flight check that
235	"the basis used matches the basis derived from the explicit formula" would
236	have caught this. The result happens to be correct (closure verified by
237	critic experiment), but on a future iteration the misspecification could
238	hide a positive signal in a different proposal.
239	
240	## Files written this session
241	
242	- `archive/ephemeral/critique_latest.md` (this file).
243	- `experiments/proposals/critique49_basis_misspec.py` + `_results.md`
244	  (corrected-basis ridge test for Proposal C).
245	- Three entries appended to `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md`.
246	
247	## Files NOT written
248	
249	- No new `novel/` files — every proposal is a strict duplicate.
250	- No new `experiments/proposals/session49_*.py` — proposer's three
251	  experiments adequately closed each path.

test window. This is why the proposer found **at most 0.4pp** gap
between analytic and ridge: that gap is finite-sample noise.

with the caveat "structure might exist at scales requiring >1000 zeros to

correlation order ≤ 2. The residual hypothesis — "could agree with GUE
pair correlation while concealing higher-order cluster structure" — had
not been individually closed.

## Single experiment

`experiments/analytic/zeta_structure/triple_correlation.py`

### Method

1. Load N=2000 non-trivial zeros (height range 14.13 .. 2515.29).
2. Unfold via Riemann-von Mangoldt smooth counting:
   `u_n = (γ_n/2π) log(γ_n/2πe) + 7/8`. Empirical mean spacing 1.0000.
3. Slide a reference zero through u; for each i with full L_max=5
   window ahead, bin all pairs (u_j − u_i, u_k − u_i) on a 2D grid.
   1995 reference zeros usable.
4. Compare to the GUE sine-kernel determinant
   `ρ_3(s_1, s_2) = 1 − K(s_1)² − K(s_2−s_1)² − K(s_2)² + 2 K(s_1) K(s_2−s_1) K(s_2)`
   with `K(t) = sin(πt)/(πt)`.

   disjoint windows of length L ∈ {1,2,4,8,16,32}.

|------|-------|-----------|---------|

| c_3 in L=1 disjoint windows | −0.000 | Poisson 1 | GUE rigidity |
| c_3 in L=8 disjoint windows | −0.001 | Poisson 8 | factor 10⁴ separation |
| c_3 in L=32 disjoint windows | +0.000 | Poisson 32 | factor 10⁴ separation |

Three independent third-order tests (bulk grid, two slices, count
cumulants) all return GUE-consistent values. The 3-point correlation
agrees with the determinantal sine-kernel prediction to within the

# State of the Art: Prime Computation (2024-2026)

Consolidated survey of all developments relevant to computing p(n) exactly.
Deduplicated from 6 overlapping source files.

Last updated: 2026-04-05 (Session 38 critique)

---

## 1. Prime Counting Algorithms

### 1.1 Combinatorial Methods (Best Practical)

**Current best asymptotic:** O(x^{2/3} / log^2 x) -- Deleglise-Rivat / Gourdon (1996/2001)

**Best implementation:** Kim Walisch's primecount library
- Version 8.4 released 2026-04-01
- Implements Gourdon's algorithm with SIMD acceleration (AVX512, ARM SVE)
- primecount 8.3 (March 2026): bidirectional clustered easy leaves, faster compression
- primecount 8.1 (January 2026): 15% faster AC.cpp
- primecount 8.0 (December 2025): new 128-bit API
- pi(10^25) computed in 330 CPU core hours on AMD EPYC Zen4
- The SIMD-accelerated Gourdon D formula in v8.4 vectorizes the hard special leaves bottleneck, estimated 2-4x speedup on modern CPUs

**Relevance to project:** This is the engine behind our best practical approach (binary search on pi(x)). Constant-factor improvements continue but no asymptotic breakthrough.

**Does it change the barrier?** No. Still O(x^{2/3}).

### 1.2 Hirsch-Kessler-Mendlovic: Elementary O~(sqrt(N)) (2022/2024)

**Source:** arXiv:2212.09857; Mathematics of Computation (2024, peer-reviewed)
**Implementation:** https://github.com/PrimeCounting/PrimeCounting (C++ and Python)

**The breakthrough:** First ELEMENTARY (non-analytic) algorithm matching the analytic
O(x^{1/2+eps}) bound for pi(x). Uses Dirichlet convolutions via NTT (Number Theoretic
Transform) to speed up the combinatorial approach from O(x^{2/3}) to O(sqrt(x) * log^{5/2} x).

**Key features:**
- No complex analysis, no zeta zeros, no arbitrary-precision complex arithmetic
- Space-time tradeoff: O~(sqrt(N)) time/space, or O~(N^{1/3}) space with O~(N^{8/15}) time
- Also improves: Mertens function to O~(sqrt(N)) (from O~(N^{0.6})), Euler totient sum, etc.

**Benchmarks (single core, Intel i3-1005G1):**
| N | Time |
|---|------|
| 10^10 | 1.23s |
| 10^12 | 14.6s |
| 10^14 | 127s |

**Practical comparison:** ~400x slower than primecount at 10^14 despite better asymptotics.
Crossover point likely around N ~ 10^{30}+, computationally unreachable for either method.

**Does it change the barrier?** No. Still O(x^{1/2+eps}) = O(2^{N/2+eps}), exponential in input bits.

### 1.3 Analytic Methods (Best Theoretical)

**Current best asymptotic:** O(x^{1/2+eps}) -- Lagarias-Odlyzko (1987)

**Implementation status:**
- Platt's method: rigorous interval arithmetic, computed pi(10^25) unconditionally
- FKBJ method: Weil-Barner explicit formula with precomputed zeta zeros, 128-bit fixed-point
- In practice, 100x slower than combinatorial methods due to zeta zero computation overhead
- ~40,000 CPU core hours for pi(10^25) vs 330 for combinatorial

**Relevance to project:** Theoretically better asymptotics but impractical constants. The 100x gap persists for all currently reachable values of x.

**Does it change the barrier?** No. O(x^{1/2+eps}) has stood since 1987.

### 1.4 Aggarwal: Complexity of Computing p(n) (October 2025)

**Source:** arXiv:2510.16285

**Key results:**
- p(n) computable in O(sqrt(n) * (log n)^4) unconditionally via binary search on pi(x)
- Conditional (RH + Cramer): O(sqrt(n) * (log n)^{7/2} * log log n)
- Proves sieve-based methods CANNOT asymptotically beat binary-search-on-pi(x)
  - Best sieve for p(n): O(n log n / log log n)
  - Binary search + pi(x): O(sqrt(n) * polylog(n))
  - Binary search wins by factor ~sqrt(n)

**Relevance:** Most rigorous recent analysis. Confirms our implemented approach (Lucy_Hedgehog/Meissel-Lehmer + binary search) is provably superior to any sieve for computing a single p(n).

**Does it change the barrier?** No new algorithm, but provides the tightest known complexity analysis.

---

## 2. Riemann Hypothesis and Zero-Density Estimates

### 2.1 Guth-Maynard: Large Value Estimates (May 2024)

**Source:** arXiv:2405.20552; published in Annals of Mathematics, 2025

**The breakthrough:**
- First improvement to Ingham's 1940 zero-density bound in 80+ years
- Improved exponent from 3/5 = 0.6 to 13/25 = 0.52
- New zero-density estimate: N(sigma, T) <= T^{30(1-sigma)/13 + o(1)}

**Propagated results:**
- PNT in short intervals: [x, x + x^{17/30}], improving from x^{3/5}
- Almost all short intervals: theta improved from 1/6 to 2/15

- Also improves: Mertens function to O~(sqrt(N)) (from O~(N^{0.6})), Euler totient sum, etc.

**Benchmarks (single core, Intel i3-1005G1):**
| N | Time |
|---|------|
| 10^10 | 1.23s |
| 10^12 | 14.6s |
| 10^14 | 127s |

**Practical comparison:** ~400x slower than primecount at 10^14 despite better asymptotics.
Crossover point likely around N ~ 10^{30}+, computationally unreachable for either method.

**Does it change the barrier?** No. Still O(x^{1/2+eps}) = O(2^{N/2+eps}), exponential in input bits.

### 1.3 Analytic Methods (Best Theoretical)

**Current best asymptotic:** O(x^{1/2+eps}) -- Lagarias-Odlyzko (1987)

**Implementation status:**
- Platt's method: rigorous interval arithmetic, computed pi(10^25) unconditionally
- FKBJ method: Weil-Barner explicit formula with precomputed zeta zeros, 128-bit fixed-point
- In practice, 100x slower than combinatorial methods due to zeta zero computation overhead
- ~40,000 CPU core hours for pi(10^25) vs 330 for combinatorial

**Relevance to project:** Theoretically better asymptotics but impractical constants. The 100x gap persists for all currently reachable values of x.

**Does it change the barrier?** No. O(x^{1/2+eps}) has stood since 1987.

### 1.4 Aggarwal: Complexity of Computing p(n) (October 2025)

**Source:** arXiv:2510.16285

**Key results:**
- p(n) computable in O(sqrt(n) * (log n)^4) unconditionally via binary search on pi(x)
- Conditional (RH + Cramer): O(sqrt(n) * (log n)^{7/2} * log log n)
- Proves sieve-based methods CANNOT asymptotically beat binary-search-on-pi(x)
  - Best sieve for p(n): O(n log n / log log n)
  - Binary search + pi(x): O(sqrt(n) * polylog(n))
  - Binary search wins by factor ~sqrt(n)

**Relevance:** Most rigorous recent analysis. Confirms our implemented approach (Lucy_Hedgehog/Meissel-Lehmer + binary search) is provably superior to any sieve for computing a single p(n).

**Does it change the barrier?** No new algorithm, but provides the tightest known complexity analysis.

---

## 2. Riemann Hypothesis and Zero-Density Estimates

### 2.1 Guth-Maynard: Large Value Estimates (May 2024)

**Source:** arXiv:2405.20552; published in Annals of Mathematics, 2025

**The breakthrough:**
- First improvement to Ingham's 1940 zero-density bound in 80+ years
- Improved exponent from 3/5 = 0.6 to 13/25 = 0.52
- New zero-density estimate: N(sigma, T) <= T^{30(1-sigma)/13 + o(1)}

**Propagated results:**
- PNT in short intervals: [x, x + x^{17/30}], improving from x^{3/5}
- Almost all short intervals: theta improved from 1/6 to 2/15

| Zero grouping/clustering | FAIL | I | Group size 2→error 9.65, group 4→0.51 (lucky), group 8→2.65 at x=10K. Rapid oscillation of exp(i*gamma*log(x)) makes each zero position essential | 29 |
| Zero clustering truncation (Proposal 21) | FAIL | I | GUE-based clustering with sinc coherence factor. 10 zeros perform as well as 200 (error saturates at O(1)). Tail prediction via GUE completely fails — tail/partial ratios swing -3.4 to +3.3. Each zero carries independent information. | 37 |
| GUE surrogate replacement | FAIL | I | Random matrix surrogates give mean=-0.81±1.18 vs actual -0.25. Right order of magnitude, wrong value. Specific zero config matters | 29 |
| Interpolation of pi correction | FAIL | I | 100 Chebyshev nodes on [2,10000]: max error=7. Fine structure from zeta zeros prevents polynomial interpolation with few points | 29 |
| Polynomial empirical correction to R(x) | FAIL | I | Polynomial in 1/log(x) reduces error 60-80% but cross-validation confirms overfitting. Oscillatory part genuinely non-polynomial | 29 |
| Compressed sensing on prime indicator | FAIL | C | pi(x)-x/log(x) has 99% energy in 1.25% of Fourier components, but those ARE zeta zero frequencies. Circular | 29 |
| Transfer matrix / stat mech for sieve | FAIL | E | State space 2^{pi(sqrt(x))}—exponential. Wheel sieve already exploits small-prime periodicity. No stat-mech shortcut | 29 |
| p-adic interpolation of pi(x) | FAIL | I | pi(x) NOT p-adically continuous: pi(x) mod p^k varies across all residue classes of x mod p^k. Local info doesn't determine global count | 29 |
| Wilson's theorem bulk primality | FAIL | E | Running factorial requires O(x!) precision. Computing (k-1)! mod k for single k is O(k). No bulk shortcut | 29 |
| Goldbach representation extraction | FAIL | C | Computing r_2(n) requires knowing primes. Hardy-Littlewood formula error O(sqrt(n/log(n))) too noisy | 29 |
| Finite field F_q[x] analogy lift | FAIL | I | F_q[x] works because its zeta has ONE zero. Z has infinitely many. No deformation from F_q to Z preserves the counting formula | 29 |
| PSLQ identity search | FAIL | I | No integer relation found among pi(x), li, R, sqrt, log, zeta values with coefficients ≤1000. Known asymptotics are the only relations | 29 |
| Primorial decomposition optimization | FAIL | E | Optimal c=3 in x^{1/c} split → O(x^{2/3}). This IS Meissel-Lehmer. No c gives better tradeoff | 29 |
| Short-interval error structure | FAIL | C | Short-interval Fourier structure from zeta zeros. CS recovery requires zero frequencies a priori | 29 |
| Number-theoretic hash p(n) mod m | FAIL | I | p(n) mod m for m≥3 shows no periodicity, no autocorrelation, pseudorandom. No polylog-computable formula | 29 |
| DE search for f(x)=pi(x)-R(x) | FAIL | I | Tested linear ODEs order<=3 poly deg<=3, Euler-type, nonlinear poly ODEs, Volterra integrals. Best linear ODE residual matches random noise (spurious from smoothing). Euler/nonlinear residuals ~1.0. f encodes infinitely many zeta-zero oscillations incompatible with finite-order DE | 29 |
| Extended PSLQ identity search x=2..100000 | FAIL | I | 14-element basis (log,sqrt,roots,li-variants,zeta zero oscillations). 18 PSLQ tests, 15 relations with nonzero f-coeff -- ALL fail cross-validation (residuals 13-53000). Functional relations f(ax) vs f(x) for a=2,3,4: fail. Shift recurrences f(x)..f(x+10): fail. Extends S19 to 10x range | 29 |
| Wilf-Zeilberger definite sum for f(x) | FAIL | I | Delta_f bimodal (prime indicator). Higher-order differences RMS GROW (ratio->2.0=white noise). Hypergeometric recurrence R^2=0.997 is spurious (trivial autocorrelation). Summation kernel full Hankel rank 250/250 (incompressible). No WZ certificate | 29 |
| f(x) vs Bernoulli numbers | FAIL | I | Bernoulli corrections < 10^{-7} at x=1000, zero correlation with f(x) (r=-0.006). Trivial zeros contribute negligibly | 29 |
| f(x) vs zeta values zeta(2..7) PSLQ | FAIL | I | PSLQ finds x-dependent relations with large coefficients (~10^6). Different coefficients at each x. Perfect-square x gives trivial sqrt relations. No universal algebraic relation | 29 |
| f(x) vs Dirichlet L-values L(1,chi) | FAIL | I | Same as zeta values -- x-dependent large-coefficient relations only. L(1,chi_3)=0.605, L(1,chi_4)=pi/4. No universal relation | 29 |
| f(x) vs Ramanujan tau function | FAIL | I | Pearson r=+0.010, p=0.93. Spearman r=+0.054. Zero correlation. Different mathematical objects (weight-12 modular form vs zeta zero oscillations) | 29 |
| Chebyshev psi(x)/log(x) as f(x) shortcut | FAIL | E | g(x)/log(x) captures 91% of f(x) variance (r=0.996) via partial summation identity. BUT psi(x) requires O(x) computation -- worse than O(x^{2/3}) sieve. Known identity, not shortcut | 29 |
| LLL minimal polynomials for f(x) | FAIL | I | "Candidate" polynomials at every x but DIFFERENT polynomials at each x (x=100: [156396,287371,96731], x=1000: [119569,141263,-381961]). Multi-point relations at float64 precision limit. f(x) values effectively algebraically independent transcendentals | 29 |
| Polynomial-in-log(x) fit for f(x) | FAIL | I | f(x) ~ sum a_j*log(x)^j: best validation RMSE=1.976 (~47% of std). With sqrt(x) factor: no improvement. Degree>4 overfits. f(x) not a polynomial in log(x) | 29 |
| Incremental delta(n) via autocorrelation | FAIL | I | r(1)=0.975 but smooth-trend artifact (after MA-10 detrending: r(1)=0.41). AR(1) RMSE=7.31, AR(5) RMSE=7.27, both >> 0.5 threshold. Only 5.3% of predictions within rounding range. H(delta(n+1)\|delta(n))=4.93 bits/step. RMSE grows with n (4.8->8.1). See experiments/proposals/critique_incremental_delta.py | 30 |
| Verification-prediction separation | FAIL | C | Primality testing is O(polylog) but ordinality (is g the n-th prime?) requires pi(g) = O(x^{2/3}). Claim conflates primality with ordinality. Local sieving gives interval count but not global rank. At x=10^100: primality ~10^9 ops, ordinality ~10^68 ops. See experiments/proposals/critique_verification_separation.py | 30 |
| NOF discrepancy for chi_P (3-party) | FAIL | - | Discrepancy HIGH (~bias), dominated by density imbalance. Trivial cylinder (A=B=C=all) achieves max. No communication lower bound. Degree-1 Walsh correlation 3-1513x random (parity), degree ≥ 2 matches random. Consistent with TC^0. See experiments/circuit_complexity/nof_discrepancy_chi_P.py | 31 |
| Gamma-2 (factorization) norm / sign-rank | FAIL | - | γ₂ ~ 2^{0.186N}, 85-93% of random matrices. Sign-rank = rank for all N=4..10. No hidden low-rank sign structure. SM complexity bound O(log γ₂) = O(N) trivially weak. F_2 rank = rank_R - 1. See experiments/circuit_complexity/gamma2_norm_chi_P.py | 31 |
| True tensor rank of chi_P (3-way) | DIAGNOSTIC | - | Tensor rank ~ d^{1.5} = 2^{N/2} = sqrt(x). N=6: rank=5 (random=7), N=9: rank≤19 (random=29), N=12: rank≈67 (random>100). chi_P 25-35% BELOW random but still EXPONENTIAL. Confirms N/2 universality. Close to generic d²/3 bound. See experiments/circuit_complexity/tensor_rank_robust.py | 31 |
| BDD size / sensitivity / decision tree | FAIL | - | BDD grows as 1.661^N (R²=0.997). chi_P ~30% simpler than random (ratio 0.69-0.71). Sensitivity = block sensitivity = certificate complexity = N for N≥7. Decision tree depth = N. All N variables essential. See experiments/circuit_complexity/min_circuit_size.py | 31 |
| F_2 correlation profile (degree-d polynomials) | DIAGNOSTIC | - | Degree-0,1 dominate: W(0)+W(1) = 47%(N=6) to 68%(N=16). W(1) z-score grows from 3 to 1513 (parity). W(d≥2) BELOW random (z-scores -2 to -30). After bias+parity removal, chi_P more pseudorandom than random. No exploitable low-degree F_2 structure. See experiments/circuit_complexity/f2_correlation_profile.py | 31 |
| Recursive prime counting (FMM-inspired) | FAIL | E | Aggressive recursion achieves O(log log x) depth but work catastrophically concentrated at depth 0: Theta(x^{2/3}/ln x). phi recursion tree has O(x^{2/3}/ln x) leaves. FMM analogy fails: no smooth kernel. Hierarchical sieve: large primes make O(x^{2/3}) irregular removals. Reduces to Meissel-Lehmer. See experiments/wildcard/recursive_prime_counting.py | 32 |
| Tropical/min-plus fast-forward via gap structure | FAIL | I | Hankel rank 418/500 (ratio to random: 0.98). Corr dim grows with embedding (2.1→5.8, no attractor). Linear R²<0.001, quadratic R²<0.002. MI(g_n;g_{n+1})=0.013 bits (0.4% of entropy). Min-plus accuracy 7-11%. Algebraic obstruction: p(n)=sum(gaps) needs (+,×) not (min,+). Gaps indistinguishable from IID. See experiments/wildcard/tropical_prime_gaps.py | 32 |
| Trace formula / moment method for zero sums | FAIL | I | Moment expansion S(x)=Σ(lnx)^k/k!·M_{k-1} DIVERGES: |M_k|~γ_max^k>>k!, radius of convergence x<1.0007. GUE trace analogy breaks: bounded eigenvalues required. Weil geometric side circular (needs all primes to x). Effective rank ~N (no compression). Gaussian damping unfavorable trade-off. 4 independent failures. See experiments/wildcard/trace_formula_approach.py | 33 |
| Contour integral evaluation of zero sum | FAIL | E | Contour ∮(ζ'/ζ)(s)·x^s/s ds equivalent to zero summation by residue theorem. Nyquist: quadrature points ≥ enclosed zeros. Smoothing trades accuracy for fewer zeros (uncertainty principle). SVD of zero-contribution matrix: 99% energy needs 133/500 components. No sparse representation in any basis. See experiments/wildcard/contour_integral_zerosum.py | 32 |
| Hybrid analytic + local sieve | FAIL | E | R⁻¹(n) error O(√p(n)) with ratio 0.05-0.25. Truncated zero sum often WORSE than none (K=0 error 12 vs K=500 error 208 at n=50000). Optimal hybrid complexity O(x^{1/2+ε}) matches Lagarias-Odlyzko. Iterative refinement oscillates. Cannot beat O(√x) zeros required. See experiments/wildcard/hybrid_analytic_sieve.py | 32 |
| Hilbert-Pólya trace / GUE model / functional equation | FAIL | E,I | GUE: correct statistics, wrong values (std≈20-60). Moments: M_k~γ_max^k diverges. Selberg trace: circular (spectral↔geometric duality). Functional equation: doesn't change kernel. δ(x) incompressible: poly deg-50 RMSE=0.21≈deg-2. 90% Fourier power needs 138/500 modes. See experiments/wildcard/hilbert_polya_trace.py | 32 |
| Convergence acceleration of zeta zero sum | FAIL | I | Richardson, Euler-Maclaurin, Padé, Cesàro, Aitken Δ², Shanks tested. Errors GROW as ~N^{0.8-1.0} (random walk). Best: Shanks(3) gives ~10x constant improvement. Root cause: each zero carries independent info (GUE-random phases). No structured error terms to exploit. See experiments/wildcard/zero_sum_acceleration.py | 32 |
| GRH batch Miller testing for pi(x) | FAIL | E | GRH Miller (witnesses ≤2ln²n) correct to 10^5. Batch testing: 1.02x speedup (negligible). Cost O(n·polylog n) — worse than sieve O(n·loglog n) and much worse than Meissel-Lehmer O(x^{2/3}). Each number requires independent modular exponentiation. See experiments/analytic/conditional/grh_miller_batch.py | 33 |
| GRH explicit formula optimal T | FAIL | E | Under GRH, need T=O(√x·log²x) zeros for error<0.5. With 1000 zeros, error≥18 for x≥10^4. Individual zeros at γ~200-400 still contribute >0.5 to pi(10^6). No way to use fewer than O(√x) zeros. Confirms Lagarias-Odlyzko at O(√x·polylog x). See experiments/analytic/conditional/grh_miller_batch.py | 33 |
| Elliott-Halberstam for pi(x) counting | FAIL | E | EH controls distribution in residue classes, not total count. Summing li(x)/φ(q) over coprime residues gives li(x) (same error as direct). Residue-class method 10^3-10^6x SLOWER than direct primepi. EH is about equidistribution, not enumeration. See experiments/analytic/conditional/elliott_halberstam_gaps.py | 33 |
| Gap structure (Cramér) for p(n) | FAIL | I | Cramér model fits well (max gaps 40-60% of ln²p). R⁻¹(n) search interval has O(ln x) primes. BUT identifying which is p(n) requires pi(x) at boundary — the counting bottleneck. At x=10^100: counting 10^57x more expensive than searching. Cramér solves wrong problem. See experiments/analytic/conditional/elliott_halberstam_gaps.py | 33 |
| Schoenfeld interval sieve under RH | FAIL | E | |pi(x)-li(x)|<√x·ln(x)/(8π). Sieve cost O(√x·ln x·ln ln x)=O(x^{1/2+ε}), better than ML O(x^{2/3}) asymptotically but still exponential in input bits. Iterative refinement with 1000 zeros: only 21% error reduction at x=10^6. Need O(√x·log²x) zeros for exactness. See experiments/analytic/conditional/schoenfeld_cramer.py | 33 |
| Cramér search + counting bottleneck | FAIL | E | Walk phase O(ln⁴x) trivial (0-114 steps verified). Counting phase pi(x₀) grows to dominate: 25% at n=5M, heading to 100%. At x=10^100: count=10^66.7 ops vs walk=10^9.5 ops. No conjecture reduces counting below O(x^{1/2+ε}). See experiments/analytic/conditional/schoenfeld_cramer.py | 33 |
| Best conditional algorithm (all conjectures) | FAIL | E | Under RH+Odlyzko-Schönhage: O(x^{1/2+ε}). RH alone with Turing zeros: O(x^{2/3+ε}), WORSE than unconditional. GRH, EH, Cramér all fail to improve beyond O(x^{1/2+ε}). For p(10^100): ~10^51 ops minimum. The √x barrier is fundamental — no standard conjecture breaks it. See experiments/analytic/conditional/best_conditional_algorithm.py | 33 |
| Spectral truncation / adaptive zero selection | FAIL | E | Select "resonant" zeros (γ·log(x) near kπ). For n<100, 1-2 zeros suffice (small-number artifact). For n≥500, 1000 zeros insufficient. Adaptive selection 41% better than sequential but cannot reduce O(√x) requirement. = reordering explicit formula sum. See experiments/proposals/proposal16_spectral_truncation_bound.py | 33 |
| p-adic lifting via CRT for pi(x) | FAIL | C+E | CRT works (3-6 primes suffice) but pi(x) mod p costs O(x^{2/3}) per prime. floor(x/d) mod q ≠ floor((x mod q)/(d mod q)) — floor division not a ring homomorphism. 12th CRT variant tested. See experiments/proposals/proposal17_padic_lifting.py | 33 |
| Dequantized Grover counting for pi(x) | FAIL | I | Tang 2024/Chia 2025 dequantization requires low-rank input. Prime indicator has adeg=N/2, comm rank=2^{N/2-1}+2 — full-rank. Truncated Möbius sums diverge. Sampling variance O(x²/S). Hyperbola=known O(√x). See experiments/proposals/proposal18_dequantized_grover_count.py | 33 |
| PSLQ/LLL on delta(n) (Ramanujan Library) | FAIL | I | delta(n) range [-130,102], std~33, lag-1 autocorr 0.95. PSLQ finds DIFFERENT relations per n (no universal formula). No recurrence order 1-6. No modular patterns. Best basis RMSE=31. 7th PSLQ/identity variant tested. See experiments/proposals/proposal19_ramanujan_library_delta.py | 33 |
| Étale cohomology point-counting for pi(x) | FAIL | C+E | Grothendieck-Lefschetz is polylog for FIXED variety, but encoding pi(x) needs unbounded dimension. Frobenius eigenvalues = zeta zeros. Character sums cost O(x). Hasse-Weil gives enough bits but each costs O(x^{2/3}). EC trace correlation 0.39 — too weak. 3rd algebraic geometry variant tested. See experiments/proposals/proposal20_etale_cohomology_count.py | 33 |

You are doing a LITERATURE WATCH for a mature prime-counting research project. The previous watch was Session 47 (~3 weeks ago). Your job is to find and report on any 2026 publications that could change the research landscape.

# CONTEXT (read first, briefly)
Read these files for context:
- /apps/aplikacijos/prime-research/CLAUDE.md (project rules)
- /apps/aplikacijos/prime-research/literature/state_of_art_2026.md (what's already known — last updated 2026-04-05)
- /apps/aplikacijos/prime-research/EDGES.md sections 0-3 (the mathematical landscape)

The project tracks the complexity of computing pi(x) and p(n). Best known: O(x^{2/3}) combinatorial (primecount), O(x^{1/2+eps}) analytic. Target: O(polylog).

# YOUR TASK
Search the web (use WebSearch and WebFetch — load them via ToolSearch if not available) for new publications since 2026-04-05 in these areas:

1. **arXiv math.NT recent submissions** for terms: "pi(x)", "prime counting function", "p_n", "nth prime", "zeta zeros", "explicit formula"
2. **ECCC TR2026** for TC^0 / NC^1 separations or matrix powering circuits
3. **Author streams** (most recent papers from):
   - Alain Connes (Connes-Consani-Moscovici operator)
   - Yakaboylu (arXiv:2408.15135 was at v15)
   - van Ittersum (partition identities for primes)
   - Ken Ono (MacMahon partition equations)
   - Kim Walisch (primecount library updates after v8.4)
   - Andrew Granville / Terence Tao (analytic number theory)
4. **GitHub releases**:
   - github.com/kimwalisch/primecount (current: v8.4 from 2026-04-01)
   - github.com/PrimeCounting/PrimeCounting

# WHAT TO REPORT
Write under 1500 words. For each finding:
- Citation (arXiv ID, journal, github tag, etc.)
- One-sentence summary
- IMPACT verdict on the project: NONE | INCREMENTAL | OPENS-NEW-PATH | BREAKTHROUGH
- If INCREMENTAL or above: specific update that should go to literature/state_of_art_2026.md

If you find nothing new — that is a valid and useful answer. The project explicitly notes "absence of news is itself information."

DO NOT write any new experiment code. DO NOT modify literature/state_of_art_2026.md yourself — just report what should be added. The main agent will integrate findings.

# OUTPUT FORMAT
Return your report directly as a brief structured markdown summary, with sections:
1. arXiv math.NT search results (window 2026-04-05 to 2026-04-26)
2. ECCC TR2026 search results  
3. Author streams check
4. GitHub release check
5. Verdict (one line: NEW-FINDINGS | NO-DELTA)
6. Recommended literature/ updates (if any)

1	# State of the Art: Prime Computation (2024-2026)
2	
3	Consolidated survey of all developments relevant to computing p(n) exactly.
4	Deduplicated from 6 overlapping source files.
5	
6	Last updated: 2026-04-05 (Session 38 critique)
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 1. Prime Counting Algorithms
11	
12	### 1.1 Combinatorial Methods (Best Practical)
13	
14	**Current best asymptotic:** O(x^{2/3} / log^2 x) -- Deleglise-Rivat / Gourdon (1996/2001)
15	
16	**Best implementation:** Kim Walisch's primecount library
17	- Version 8.4 released 2026-04-01
18	- Implements Gourdon's algorithm with SIMD acceleration (AVX512, ARM SVE)
19	- primecount 8.3 (March 2026): bidirectional clustered easy leaves, faster compression
20	- primecount 8.1 (January 2026): 15% faster AC.cpp
21	- primecount 8.0 (December 2025): new 128-bit API
22	- pi(10^25) computed in 330 CPU core hours on AMD EPYC Zen4
23	- The SIMD-accelerated Gourdon D formula in v8.4 vectorizes the hard special leaves bottleneck, estimated 2-4x speedup on modern CPUs
24	
25	**Relevance to project:** This is the engine behind our best practical approach (binary search on pi(x)). Constant-factor improvements continue but no asymptotic breakthrough.
26	
27	**Does it change the barrier?** No. Still O(x^{2/3}).
28	
29	### 1.2 Hirsch-Kessler-Mendlovic: Elementary O~(sqrt(N)) (2022/2024)
30	
31	**Source:** arXiv:2212.09857; Mathematics of Computation (2024, peer-reviewed)
32	**Implementation:** https://github.com/PrimeCounting/PrimeCounting (C++ and Python)
33	
34	**The breakthrough:** First ELEMENTARY (non-analytic) algorithm matching the analytic
35	O(x^{1/2+eps}) bound for pi(x). Uses Dirichlet convolutions via NTT (Number Theoretic
36	Transform) to speed up the combinatorial approach from O(x^{2/3}) to O(sqrt(x) * log^{5/2} x).
37	
38	**Key features:**
39	- No complex analysis, no zeta zeros, no arbitrary-precision complex arithmetic
40	- Space-time tradeoff: O~(sqrt(N)) time/space, or O~(N^{1/3}) space with O~(N^{8/15}) time
41	- Also improves: Mertens function to O~(sqrt(N)) (from O~(N^{0.6})), Euler totient sum, etc.
42	
43	**Benchmarks (single core, Intel i3-1005G1):**
44	| N | Time |
45	|---|------|
